title: The Guru Panth
hookLine: the collective Khalsa carries the Guru's authority with the Granth

cards: A question has split the community. Should it do this, or that? Nobody is sure, and opinions are loud.
So people gather, the Guru Granth Sahib open at the front. They talk it through, not in a back office but before the Granth. Ardas is said.

A decision is reached together, and announced as something more than a vote. In Sikh life, a decision made by the gathered Khalsa in the Guru's presence can carry the Guru's weight. How can ordinary people hold that?

teach.h: PANTH: A PATH, AND ITS PEOPLE.
teach.b: Panth means a path, and so the people who walk it together. Guru Panth is the Khalsa community as Guru.
Tradition says that before Guru Gobind Singh died, he ended the line of human Gurus and placed the Guru in two forms: the Guru Granth Sahib, the Word, and the Guru Panth, the community of the Khalsa.
Sikhs speak of them together: Guru Granth, Guru Panth. The Granth holds the teaching; the Panth carries it out, decides together, and acts. Neither stands alone.
A Panth that ignored the Granth would be a crowd with opinions; a Granth with no Panth would be a book no one lives. The Sikh Rehat Maryada gives this a working form.
In paraphrase: a gurmata, a resolution made with the Guru's assent, is passed by a gathering of the Panth in the presence of the Guru Granth Sahib, on questions that bear on the Gurus' teaching.
A gurmata can't overrule Gurbani; it applies it. One story Sikhs tell shows the idea in a single scene.
When the Tenth Guru founded the Khalsa, he initiated the first Five, and then, tradition says, asked them to initiate him. The Guru stood before his own disciples to receive what he had just given.
The teacher put himself inside the community he had made.
That's the Guru Panth in a picture: authority living not in one person at the top but in the gathered people, bowed before the Word.

how: Sikhs speak of Guru Granth and Guru Panth together; on questions bearing on the Gurus' teaching, a gathering of the Panth may pass a gurmata, a resolution made in the presence of the Guru Granth Sahib and in keeping with Gurbani.

games.q: you've just initiated the first Five of the Khalsa. tradition says the Tenth Guru did what next?
o: asked the Five to initiate him.
sent them away to found their own groups.
games.why: tradition says the Guru asked his new disciples to initiate him: the teacher placed himself inside the community he made.

practice: Picture the people you belong with, a congregation, a family, a team, friends, gathered in one room, and notice that none of them carries the whole thing alone, and neither do you.
Rest there as one among them, not the one in charge, and if you pray, hold them all before Waheguru.
